components.description: Auburn's university-wide FMLA policy: up to 12 weeks of job-protected unpaid leave in a rolling 12-month period for the employee's own serious health condition (including pregnancy incapacity), the birth of a child and bonding, adoption or foster placement, or care of a seriously ill family member; restates the federal FMLA. Accrued sick leave must be used before the leave becomes leave without pay; paid balances run concurrently (c2). Spouses both employed by Auburn each receive up to 12 weeks.
components.mechanism_note: Statutory leave (FMLA) restated by the university policy without added length (schema statute_source).
components.faculty_group_note: "This policy applies to all eligible employees."
components.eligible_parent_wording: "Birth of an employee's child(ren), bonding with newborn or newly placed child, adoption ... foster care"; own serious health condition (birth parent, U5); care of spouse with a serious health condition (non-birth parent, U5)
components.dual_employee_rule: each may take (both spouses employed by Auburn: each entitled to up to 12 weeks for birth, newborn care, adoption or foster placement)
components.entitlement_note: "is entitled to take"; a statutory entitlement stays guaranteed (schema).
components.duration_note: Policy: 'up to 12 weeks' in a rolling 12-month period; statute: 'a total of 12 workweeks'. Intermittent leave for birth or adoption requires the supervisor's approval.
components.medical_certification_note: Required for leave for the employee's own serious health condition or to care for a family member's serious health condition; no certification stated for birth or bonding leave.
components.relief_note: Formal leave of absence; no relief stated (R9).
components.time_window: leaves for birth or adoption must be taken within 12 months of the event
components.notice: 30-day notice if the leave is foreseeable; otherwise as much notice as practicable

notes: Governing documents: the Faculty Handbook chapter 3 (a faculty handbook holding the tenure-clock provisions, 3.6.4) and the university Family and Medical Leave Policy (a leave policy for all eligible employees) both cover tenure-stream faculty, so the rule for records with no governing document (reader instructions §3) does not apply and missing is false. Neither saved source contains a parental, maternity, childbirth, modified-duties or paid-leave provision; the only birth leave found is FMLA (c1).

The handbook chapter contains no leave provisions other than professional improvement leave (3.8.1, with and without pay), external residential fellowships (3.8.2) and the tenure-clock provisions (3.6.4). Professional improvement leave serves professional development only and is not a component (a parent could not take it for a birth).

Cited but not saved: FMLA policy section VII 'Family and Medical Leave Act Procedures'; the 'established leave policy' governing sick, annual and compensatory leave (accrual rates and maxima unknown); the 'Salary Continuation Plan' and 'On-Job Injury Program' (named as running concurrently with FMLA; their terms, payer and any childbirth period are unknown, so no component was created for the Salary Continuation Plan: flagged on c2); the dependent eligibility matrix; the leave of absence without pay policy referred to in Handbook 3.6.4; the ADA Accommodations Policy and other workplace policies listed in Handbook 3.2.1 (not leave).

Version: the FMLA policy is marked 'EFFECTIVE DATE February 2018' with no day, so it may postdate the reference date 2018-02-22; its terms restate the federal FMLA (12 weeks, 12 months and 1,250 hours), which was in force on that date. Components citing it carry version_uncertain. The handbook page shows 'Last Updated: March 08, 2018' (capture 2018-03-17); read as in force on 2018-02-22 per its version note.

must_exhaust_first ['sick'] is recorded on c2 (the balances) rather than on c1: FMLA leave starts at onset whatever the balances; the policy requires accrued sick leave to be used before the leave becomes leave without pay.

Dual-employee rule: the policy lets spouses both employed by Auburn each take up to 12 weeks for a birth or placement, more than the statute's combined limit (29 U.S.C. 2612(f)); recorded in c1 dual_employee_rule.

Chain, birth parent: FMLA leave 12 weeks (c1; own sick, annual or compensatory balances within it from the onset, c2) ; tenure-clock extension of one year available on request (c3); leave without pay time may be excluded from the tenure clock (c4, general purpose).
Chain, non-birth parent: FMLA leave 12 weeks (c1; own balances within it, c2); tenure-clock extension of one year (c3).
